parser.error_behavior: Short/invalid frames that pass the length check but are too short for a window throw RangeError('byteOffset') from the inlined bounds checks (0x8e3918, 0x8e3960, 0x8e39a8, 0x8e39f0 -> AllocateRangeErrorStub 0x3d81d4, RangeError.range 0x3d7960, ThrowStub 0xa747f8). There is no try/catch in the closure and no checksum error handling.

press_release: No event typing: the D2 stream is a periodic full-state report (live ~20 Hz), so press and release are just bit set/clear transitions inside the mask. The listener writes the derived boolean per key into _RainbowTestState current-state fields (0x1f,0x27,...,0xbf) and compares each pair against the previous snapshot (0x1b,0x23,...,0xbb); on any change it copies current->previous (0x8e3670-0x8e3760) and calls State::setState (0x8e37d8). Analog values are treated the same way with a |delta| > 327.68 (double) threshold (0x8e380c-0x8e38b4) before the second setState (0x8e3900). No debounce, no edge logging, no separate key-down/key-up frames.

CONTRADICTED: 'the Button Test parser gates on the opcode byte (0x02)'. The listener contains no comparison against 2; its only frame gate is frame[1]==18. (Other pages do gate on byte[2]: rainbow_root expects 239, configs_config expects 215.)
CONTRADICTED: 'the app verifies the frame checksum before parsing'. No byte-sum code exists in the listener; getCheckSum/getCRC exist only for TX frames (gamepadset.dart 0x79c368 / 0x3d2664).

CONTRADICTED: 'the app ignores the first status event after D2 ON'. There is no first-frame flag; state is initialised to false/0 and a first frame carrying any pressed key or non-zero analog triggers setState.
CONTRADICTED: 'the D2 acknowledgement echo is consumed by the app'. The 5-byte echo cannot pass the frame[1]==18 gate and is dropped at 0x8e2460.

CONTRADICTED: 'the key mask is little-endian over bytes[3..6] (bit id 0 in byte[3])'. The decode swizzle makes frame[3] the most significant byte, so ids 0-7 sit in frame[6]; this matches the gamepadset constants (e.g. keyL1 = 0x40 = bit 6 = LB) and the live byte->id table.
CONTRADICTED (for this page): 'the Button Test listener reads an 8-byte key field 3..10 as rainbow_root does'. The Button Test listener reads exactly 4 bytes at 3..6 plus four 2-byte analog windows.

CONTRADICTED: 'the disable frame is sent unconditionally on leaving the page'. dispose sends it only when the connection state is still 'connected' (Obj!DeviceConnectionState@8fcb51, objs.txt line 20559).
